checklist: Verify your contractor license is current and valid in AZ
Confirm your liability insurance is active (certificate is conditional only when the listed condition applies at permit office)
Have the property address and legal parcel number ready
Know the project value/cost — required on most permit applications

Confirm the required license is active and matches the application: Arizona ROC-licensed HVAC contractor pulls the permit on the homeowner’s behalf, and the contractor’s ROC license number must appear on the application. Phoenix also requires separate City Contractor Registration on top of the ROC license before the permit will be accepted.
Bring 2 copies of all documents to City of Phoenix Planning & Development Department (PDD)
response_body.city_contractor_registration: Phoenix requires separate City Contractor Registration in addition to the Arizona ROC license. Verify the registration is current before applying; an expired city registration can block the permit. Renewal is city-controlled and should be checked before each permit submission.

common_mistakes: Submitting the permit without current Phoenix City Contractor Registration — Phoenix will reject the application even if the ROC license is valid
Trying to pull separate mechanical and electrical permits when the job qualifies for Phoenix’s combined residential HVAC permit system
Starting work before the permit is issued and posted on site — Phoenix can issue a stop-work order
Not confirming whether the disconnect, breaker, or circuit is being changed — that can trigger additional electrical review
Using the wrong portal route or assuming the old HVAC fee is still current without checking the live Phoenix PDD schedule

response_body.inspection_booking: Schedule inspections through the City of Phoenix PDD online portal at. Phoenix requires a minimum 24-hour advance notice; same-day requests are not accepted. Phone: (602) 262-7811. Use the permit number to request the inspection and confirm the job is ready before booking.

inspections.description: Inspector checks that the condenser and air handler match the approved scope, equipment is properly set and secured, disconnect is installed and accessible, refrigerant lines are supported and sealed, condensate drain is sloped and trapped correctly, clearances are maintained, and the system operates safely after startup.
inspections.timing: After equipment is installed, wiring and refrigerant work are complete, and before the job is closed out

inspections.description: If any electrical work was changed, inspector checks breaker sizing, disconnect location, conductor sizing, grounding/bonding, and that the equipment is properly connected to the existing circuit or new circuit as approved.

pro_tips: Check your Phoenix contractor registration renewal date before starting any permit application — registration lapses are one of the most avoidable rejection reasons
Phoenix uses a single-permit system for many residential trade combos, so verify whether your HVAC replacement can stay under one combined permit before opening separate trade applications

Book the inspection at least 24 hours ahead and make sure the system is fully installed and operational before the inspector arrives
